scope: DFW suburbs (Collin, Denton, Rockwall, Kaufman, Ellis, Johnson) - health & opportunity

records.name: McKinney Workforce Center
records.organization: Workforce Solutions for North Central Texas
records.description_en: Free help finding a job, writing a resume, and getting job training. Staff can also help with child care help for working parents.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to job seekers. Some training programs have their own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the center during open hours or call. You can also start online at dfwjobs.com.

records.name: Child Care Scholarships (Child Care Services)
records.organization: Workforce Solutions for North Central Texas
records.description_en: Helps low-income families pay for child care so parents can work or go to school.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income families. Parents must work, go to school, or train at least 25 hours a week on average (50 hours for two-parent families). Income limits start at $5,216 a month for a family of 2.
documents_needed: Proof you live in the service area
Proof of U.S. citizenship or legal immigration status for each child
Pay stubs for the last 13 weeks for all working household members
School or training details (school name, enrollment hours, transcript) if in school
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Texas child care scholarship application. Call Child Care Services with questions.
records.cost: Free to apply; families may owe a parent share of cost
records.notes: Income limit table on source goes from $5,216/month (family of 2) to $11,045/month (family of 10). Child Care Services phone taken from dfwjobs.com/contactus. Board covers 14 counties total. Parent share of cost not confirmed on source page.

records.name: LifePath Systems Behavioral Health and Crisis Services
records.description_en: Mental health care, crisis help, youth and family services, veteran support, and services for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities. The crisis line is open 24/7.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Collin County with mental health, intellectual, or developmental challenges. Anyone in crisis can call the crisis line.
records.how_to_apply: In a crisis, call 1-877-422-5939 any time. For regular care, call Behavioral Health at (972) 422-5939.
records.notes: 24/7 Crisis Line: 1-877-422-5939 (TRS 711). Behavioral health toll free: 1-844-544-5939. Early Childhood Intervention: (972) 562-0331. IDD: (972) 727-9133. Address is the administration office; clinics in McKinney, Plano, Allen, Forney. Collin County Local Mental Health Authority.

records.name: Denton County MHMR Center (My Health My Resources)
records.description_en: Mental health care for adults and children, substance use help, and disability services. It has a 24/7 crisis line, mobile crisis team, and a walk-in psychiatric triage center.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Denton County. Anyone in a mental health crisis can call the crisis line.
records.how_to_apply: In a crisis, call 1-800-762-0157 or 988. For services, call (940) 381-5000 for intake.
records.hours: Monday-Friday 8a-5p, Flexible Hours Available; crisis line 24/7
records.notes: Crisis hotline 1-800-762-0157 (24/7). Psychiatric Triage Facility walk-in assessments: (940) 381-9965. Toll-free main: 1-800-942-5808. Mailing: PO Box 2346, Denton, TX 76202. Denton County Local Mental Health Authority.

records.name: Lakes Regional Community Center Crisis and Mental Health Services
records.description_en: Mental health, substance use, and disability services, with a 24/7 crisis line for Hunt, Kaufman, and Rockwall counties.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who live in Kaufman or Rockwall County (and other counties Lakes Regional serves). Anyone in crisis can call.
records.how_to_apply: In a crisis, call 866-260-8000 any time. For non-emergency help, call 877-505-2537.
records.notes: Crisis line for Hunt, Kaufman and Rockwall Counties: 866-260-8000. Local office addresses were not confirmed.

records.name: Pecan Valley Centers - Cleburne Clinic
records.organization: Pecan Valley Centers for Behavioral & Developmental HealthCare
records.description_en: Mental health assessment, referral, and outpatient care for adults, children, and teens. A 24/7 crisis hotline and mobile crisis team are available.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who live in Johnson County and nearby counties Pecan Valley serves.
records.how_to_apply: Call the crisis and intake line at 1-800-772-5987, or call the Cleburne clinic.
records.hours: 8-5 PM; late hours 8-7 PM every Tuesday
records.notes: 24/7 Mental Health Crisis Hotline & Intake Screening: 1-800-772-5987 (confirmed on pecanvalley.org/crisis-services). Pecan Valley serves Johnson, Somervell, Hood, Erath, Parker, and Palo Pinto counties.

records.name: North Texas Behavioral Health Authority (NTBHA)
records.description_en: Connects people to public mental health and substance use care, with care coordinators for Ellis and nearby counties.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For residents of Dallas, Ellis, Hunt, Kaufman, Navarro, and Rockwall counties who need behavioral health care.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text 214-366-9407, or call toll free 877-653-6363. Ellis County residents can call the South and East care coordinators at (469) 780-9159.
records.notes: Crisis lines listed: (866) 260-8000 or (844) 672-5700. Ellis County care coordinators email: SouthandEastCareCoordinators@ntbha.org. Physical address not listed on source.

records.name: Collin County Indigent Health Program
records.description_en: Helps pay for health care for low-income adults in Collin County who qualify.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adult Collin County residents with low income and few resources. You must show proof of income and resources.
documents_needed: Other supporting documents listed on the application
records.how_to_apply: Apply online, by mail, or drop off the form in person. A decision is made within 14 business days after a complete application.
records.hours: Monday - Thursday 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM (Closed Friday - Sunday)
records.notes: Source says program is for 'qualified, adult indigent residents'; min_age 18 inferred from 'adult'. Exact income limit not stated on page.

records.name: Collin County WIC Program
records.description_en: Healthy food benefits, nutrition classes, and breastfeeding help for pregnant women, new moms, and kids under 5.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant or breastfeeding women, women who had a baby in the last 6 months, and children under 5. Income must be at or below 185% of the poverty level, or you get Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF.
documents_needed: Proof of income for all household members
records.how_to_apply: Request a first appointment at texaswic.org, call your nearest office, or text 85511.
records.hours: Mon & Wed 8 a.m.-5 p.m.; Tue & Thu 8 a.m.-5:30 p.m.; Fri 8 a.m.-1 p.m.
records.notes: Second clinic: 900 E. Park Blvd., Plano, TX 75074, (972) 633-3350, same hours.

records.name: Collin County Immunizations Clinic
records.description_en: Vaccines for eligible children and adults.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For eligible children and adults. Call to check if you qualify.
records.how_to_apply: Call to make an appointment. Walk-ins are not listed; the clinic is by appointment only.
records.notes: Same building also has TB clinic (Mon-Fri 8:30 a.m.-5 p.m.) and STD/HIV clinic.

records.name: Denton County Public Health Clinical Services
records.description_en: Low-cost primary care, dental care, shots, women's health, and STI/HIV and TB testing at two county clinics.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Eligibility is based on income, resources, where you live, and who is in your household. Shots are offered to people without a regular doctor.
records.how_to_apply: Call to schedule an eligibility screening appointment.
records.hours: Monday through Friday 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
records.cost: Based on eligibility; call for details
records.notes: Lewisville clinic: 190 N Valley Parkway, Lewisville, TX 75067, (972) 434-4700, same hours. Public Health page says vaccines are offered walk-in for people without a medical home.

records.name: Denton County WIC
records.description_en: Healthy food benefits and nutrition help for pregnant women, new moms, and young children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant women, new mothers, and young children who meet Texas WIC income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Apply at texaswic.org or call any Denton County WIC clinic.
records.notes: Other clinics (same phone and hours): 190 N Valley Parkway, Lewisville 75067; 3024 E Hebron Pkwy, Carrollton 75010.

records.name: Kaufman County Indigent Health Care Program
records.description_en: Helps pay for needed medical care for very low-income Kaufman County residents.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Kaufman County residents with monthly net income at or below 21% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines and resources under $2,000 ($3,000 if aged/disabled in some households). You must have a medical need.
records.how_to_apply: Download the English or Spanish application from the county website, or call or visit the office.
records.notes: Email: indigenthealth@kaufmancounty.net. Fax 469-595-0496. Spanish spoken.

records.name: CommonGood Medical (formerly Hope Clinic of McKinney)
records.description_en: A faith-based clinic that gives medical care and support to uninsured adults in Collin County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Collin County residents with no insurance (no Medicaid, Medicare, or other coverage) who meet household income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call the McKinney clinic to ask about becoming a patient.
records.hours: Weekdays 8:30 AM - 5 PM (closed noon-1 PM); 10 AM - 3 PM third Saturday
records.notes: hopeclinicmckinney.org redirects to commongoodmedical.org. Farmersville clinic Fridays 8:30 AM-4 PM at 206 N. Main St. (First United Methodist Church), Farmersville 75442. Exact income limit not confirmed.

records.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas - McKinney Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as family law, housing, and benefits problems.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents with a civil (not criminal) case. You likely qualify if you get SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, WIC, or live in public housing.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Legal Aid Line at 1-888-529-5277, apply online, or visit the office. Call the local office if you have a court deadline or were served with a lawsuit.
records.notes: Toll-free: 866-511-8018. Legal Aid Line 888-529-5277 (8 a.m.-5 p.m. Mon-Fri per main site). Some exceptions for immigrant survivors (U/T visa, VAWA). Office hours not listed.

records.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas - Denton Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as family law, housing, and benefits problems.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents with a civil (not criminal) case. You likely qualify if you get SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, WIC, or live in public housing.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Legal Aid Line at 1-888-529-5277, apply online, or visit the office.
records.notes: Toll-free: 800-955-1407. Office hours not listed.

records.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas - Waxahachie Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as family law, housing, and benefits problems.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents with a civil (not criminal) case. You likely qualify if you get SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, WIC, or live in public housing.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Legal Aid Line at 1-888-529-5277, apply online, or visit the office.
records.notes: Toll-free: 866-614-3344. Office hours not listed.

records.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas Landlord-Tenant Line
records.description_en: Free legal help line for renters with landlord problems, like eviction or repairs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income renters in counties served by Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas.
records.how_to_apply: Call the landlord-tenant line at 855-548-8457.
records.notes: LANWT serves 114 counties in North and West Texas; only Collin, Denton and Ellis are confirmed here via local offices. Johnson, Kaufman and Rockwall residents should call 1-888-529-5277 to confirm. Hours not listed for this line.

records.name: The Samaritan Inn Housing Program
records.description_en: Shelter and a housing program for people who are homeless, with case management, free counseling, job help, and money classes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For homeless men, women, and families with children. You must be drug and alcohol free for 30 days, have no violent offenses, and be willing to work full-time (part-time if disabled).
records.how_to_apply: Come to an intake interview on Tuesdays, Thursdays, or Sundays from 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM. First come, first served.
records.hours: Intake: Tuesdays, Thursdays & Sundays 8:00 AM - 1:00 PM
records.notes: Violent offenses over 10 years old may be considered. Email info@saminn.org. Collin County service area inferred from McKinney location.

records.name: Minnie's Food Pantry
records.description_en: Free groceries by drive-thru, plus walk-up help for people who are homeless and a free clothing boutique.
records.eligibility_summary_en: No one is turned away at the drive-thru. The boutique needs an intake appointment and proof of low income.
records.how_to_apply: Drive through during open hours; households may come once a month. Walk-up guests experiencing homelessness may come weekly.
records.notes: Boutique at 651 18th Street.

records.name: Frisco Family Services
records.description_en: Emergency money help, a food market, seasonal help like back-to-school and holiday programs, and life skills classes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the Frisco and Frisco ISD community. Call to check if you qualify.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the main office during business hours.
records.hours: Office & Food Market: M-F, 9 AM-5 PM
records.notes: Food Market at 9085 Dogwood St. Frisco spans Collin and Denton counties. Formal residency rules not stated on homepage.

records.name: All Community Outreach (ACO)
records.description_en: Food and essentials, help with rent and utility bills, and career and education programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves Collin County neighbors in need. Call to check eligibility.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit during open hours.
records.hours: Mon, Wed-Fri 9:00 AM-4:00 PM; Tue 9:00 AM-6:00 PM
records.notes: Specific eligibility rules not listed on homepage.

records.name: Christian Community Action (CCA)
records.description_en: A food market, job and education programs, kids' programs like Kids Eat Free, senior services, and counseling.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves low-income residents of Denton County. Call to check eligibility.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the Lewisville office.
records.notes: Hours not listed on homepage. Faith-based organization.

records.name: Interfaith Ministries of Denton Emergency Assistance
records.description_en: Emergency help with utility bills, diapers, hygiene items, and DCTA bus passes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Denton-area residents with income at or below 80% of area median income who have a sudden, documented crisis they did not cause.
records.how_to_apply: Send an information request through their website contact form, or call. This first step is not the application.
records.hours: Mon-Thu 9:00 AM-4:00 PM (closed 1-2 PM); Fri 9:00 AM-1:00 PM
records.notes: No rental assistance program. Email info@ifmdenton.org.

records.name: Denton County Friends of the Family
records.organization: Denton County Friends of the Family
records.description_en: Emergency shelter, counseling, legal advocacy, and support for people hurt by domestic violence, rape, or sexual abuse.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For survivors of domestic violence, rape, and sexual abuse and their children in Denton County.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour crisis hotline at 940-382-7273.
records.notes: Phone listed is the 24-hour crisis hotline.

records.name: DCTA Reduced Fare Program
records.description_en: Lower bus and train fares for seniors, people with disabilities, Medicare cardholders, and students.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people 65 or older, people with disabilities, Medicare cardholders, and students 6-18 with a student ID. Children 5 and under ride free.
documents_needed: Proof of eligibility (age, disability, Medicare card, or student ID)
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the DCTA Reduced Fare application (English, Spanish, or Hakha Chin) to get a Reduced Fare Eligible badge. Call with questions.
records.notes: The badge is not a pass; riders still pay the reduced fare. DCTA also has a Non-Profit Pass Program. No general low-income fare confirmed on the reduced fare page.
